episodes.173259: Increasing atmospheric moisture combined with upper level energy to produce locally heavy rain and flooding.
episodes.173267: Strong thunderstorms tracking along a cold front produced gusty winds as they tracked over the Lake Michigan waters during the late morning and early afternoon hours on Wednesday (10/12).
episodes.173283: Two lines of strong thunderstorms pushed southeast across the region.  The first during the late afternoon and early evening hours, and the second during the mid to late evenign hours. Both lines resulted in isolated wind damage.
episodes.173288: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours ahead of an approaching cold front.
episodes.173393: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into eastern Oklahoma during the morning hours of the 12th, as a cold front moved into the area. The strongest storms produced large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.173394: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into northwestern Arkansas during the morning hours of the 12th, as a cold front moved into the area. The strongest storms produced large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.173488: Strong to severe storms moved from northwest to southeast ahead of an approaching front during the morning of the 12th. A few storms with this round were strong enough to produce quarter to half-dollar sized hail near Fort Scott.
episodes.173489: Strong to severe storms moved from northwest to southeast ahead of an approaching front during the morning of the 12th. A few storms with this round were strong enough to produce quarter to half-dollar sized hail near Springfield.
episodes.173500: Storms developed along a cold front producing widespread wind gust reports. Peak reported wind gust was 87 mph.
episodes.173555: A cold front moving through southern Wisconsin was the focus for tornadic development through the lunch hour.  Temperatures and dew points rose enough in the late morning to help fuel the strengthening of the rain along the front.  There were numerous tornadic debris signatures that developed, many of which appeared to be extremely brief which did no damage outside of lofting leaves into the air.  The main tornado for this event was the one that went through West Allis which mainly did tree damage as it came through.  No lightning was observed through this event.
episodes.173637: A coastal trough over the local Atlantic waters approached the local Atlantic coast during the pre-dawn hours which shifted bands of heavy rainfall onshore. Convergence along the trough axis and lift from central FL ahead of an approaching warm front combined with high tropical moisture (PWATs 1.7 to 2 inches) under SW flow aloft produced localized heavy rainfall.
episodes.173645: Outflow from a line of thunderstorms moving through the region produced a brief period of strong wind gusts over portions of Lake Superior on the morning of the 12th.
episodes.173649: Storm force west wind gusts developed at Minneapolis Shoal Light in the wake of a cold frontal passage on 10/12.
episodes.173816: A few strong storms developed ahead of a cold front due to a marginal combination of instability and wind shear.  One stormed downed a few trees in Randolph county, resulting in a few power outages.
episodes.174047: As a cold front entered into the Ohio Valley on the evening of October 12th, showers and a few thunderstorms preceded the boundary across southeast Ohio. A few of these storms reached strengths that supported strong winds and large hail. The local emergency manager of Lawrence County observed quarter sized hail near the Coal Grove township early that evening.
episodes.174048: A cold front moved through Arkansas and brought severe thunderstorms to the state.
episodes.174126: A storm system approaching middle Tennessee from the Great Plains along with moist southerly surface flow combined to produce scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms over the area on October 12, 2022. Ahead of this approaching storm system, the atmosphere was supportive for strong to severe thunderstorms, especially across southern portions of middle Tennessee where modest instability was present along with strong wind shear values. This event produced widespread severe thunderstorm winds and wind damage with the most significant damage found in Manchester due to an intense microburst.
episodes.174148: On the afternoon of October 12th, warm and moist air was in place ahead of a potent cold front. Isolated to scattered showers and storms developed in the open warm sector ahead of the front. In the presence of limited low level shear but adequate deep layer shear, some storms took on supercellular characteristics with large hail and damaging winds closer to the cold front and brought an additional round of strong, damaging winds into the overnight.
episodes.174262: A longwave trough progressed east from the Plains into the Mid-Mississippi Valley during the day on October 12th, which reinforced a cold front southeast into East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon. Above normal temperatures and humidity for mid-October was observed ahead of the front, which focused an area of moderate instability across Southern Arkansas and North Louisiana, as large scale forcing increased ahead of the approaching trough axis. This resulted in the development of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of North-Central Louisiana and Southern Arkansas during the late afternoon and evening hours, with multiple reports of large hail and isolated wind damage before diminishing with the frontal passage late that night.
episodes.174379: A line of convective showers moved across far northeast Illinois during the early afternoon of October 12th producing isolated wind damage.
episodes.174510: Scattered storms developed across central Minnesota during the late afternoon and evening. Most reports of hail were for 1/2 inch or smaller, but one storm in eastern Morrison County had a report of 3/4 inch hail.
episodes.174519: Instability across the islands generated a couple of days of  showers, with brief periods of locally heavy rainfall, across portions of the Big Island, Kauai and Maui. No injuries or damages were noted from this event.
episodes.174678: Weak low pressure to the southeast wrapped in enough moisture to fuel isolated thunderstorms over southern San Bernardino County. One storm produced flash flooding.
episodes.174704: An upper-level trough and attendant cold front rotated through the region during the afternoon and evening of October 12, 2022. The cold front interacted with a moist and unstable airmass to produce numerous thunderstorms across West Tennessee and north Mississippi. Several storms were severe with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.174705: An upper-level trough and attendant cold front rotated through the region during the afternoon and evening of October 12, 2022. The cold front interacted with a moist and unstable airmass to produce numerous thunderstorms across West Tennessee and north Mississippi. Several storms were severe with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.174752: A cold front moving through the region on the morning of October 12th produced a few strong to marginally severe storms.
episodes.174754: Thunderstorms occurred across Southern California October 11-12. Heavy rain was reported on October 11, mainly across the San Bernardino County Mountains and northern San Diego County. More widespread impacts were felt on October 12, with reports of heavy rain, accumulating small hail and several debris flows near the Fairview Fire burn scar.
episodes.174806: A cold front moving through southern Wisconsin and out across the southern half of Lake Michigan. As the squall moved closer to the shoreline of Lake Michigan, significant thunderstorm winds brought tree damage all the way to the shoreline in the Milwaukee area.
episodes.174821: During the afternoon and evening hours on October 12th, a mid- and upper-level trough and associated surface cold front moved across central Kentucky. Ahead of the front, temperatures warmed into the low-to-mid 80s, with dewpoints remaining fairly modest in the upper 50s and lower 60s. This contributed to around 1000-1500 J/kg SBCAPE and MUCAPE in the pre-frontal environment. The instability ahead of the front combined with approximately 40 knots of effective bulk shear to produce two waves of strong-to-severe storms across Kentucky. The first wave of storms were more discrete and cellular in nature, producing sub-severe hail across Russell County. The second and more potent wave of storms was a quasi-linear convective system which developed along the surface boundary, brining damaging straight-line winds to portions of Metcalfe County.
episodes.174931: An isolated thunderstorm embedded within widespread rain across eastern Iowa. produced penny sized hail in Lee County Iowa.
episodes.174970: A warm front lifted into the region during the morning hours of the 11th bringing unseasonably warm temperatures into the Northland for the afternoon hours. The associated cold front arrived for the evening and overnight hours and led to the development of showers and thunderstorms. While most remained below severe levels, one storm that moved across northern St. Louis County did produce hail to the size of golf balls.
episodes.174971: A warm front lifted into the region during the morning hours of the 11th bringing unseasonably warm temperatures into the Northland for the afternoon hours. The associated cold front arrived for the evening and overnight hours and led to the development of showers and thunderstorms. While most remained below severe levels, one storm that moved across Douglas County did produce hail to the size of pennies.
episodes.175003: A warm front lifted north across the region producing isolated thunderstorms. One storm produced hail in Central Louisiana.
episodes.175064: A short wave trough digging southward towards the Central Gulf Coast states provided ample lift for the development of convection. Moderate levels of mid level shear and instability aided in the intensity of the thunderstorms, producing several rounds of severe thunderstorms throughout the day.
episodes.175066: A thin line of thunderstorms developed west of Lake Michigan during the morning of 10-12, eventually tracking across the lake and over northern Michigan. This line of storms ended up producing a 60 mph wind gust in Roscommon county.
episodes.175095: A strong troughing pattern was in place across the central Conus, with enhanced SW to NE flow present across the Ohio Valley during the day on October 12. A surface low pressure system was also slowly passing across the Hudson Bay during the day, dragging a long cold front south and southeastward. This front was slow moving, staying east of the Commonwealth through much of the day. The increased SW flow across the region helped to advect both moisture and warmer temperatures into the region, ultimately leading to destabilization. Storms began developing well ahead of the front, impacting portions of central and eastern Kentucky. The short term forecaster on the desk at JKL noted that: In recent |mesoanalysis and collaboration with the SPC, there's modest |effective shear around 30 to 40 knots, ideal curving within the |hodograph and modest CAPE values for October. All which have been |reflected by the SPC's Day 1 Marginal Risk with 2 percent |categorical tornado and 5 percent categorical wind threats. ||Sure enough, these storms increased in strength, leading to multiple warnings during the early and mid afternoon. Two of these storms did end up producing decent winds, resulting in downed trees across portions of Magoffin and Bath County. Bath County faired the worst, with multiple barns also being destroyed in the severe winds.

A peg construction barn collapsed with most debris uniformly laying towards the ENE and NE. The roof was dislodged and tossed 150 feet to the east of the barn, but the framing of the roof seemed to be rotted. The cement footers that the bar was sitting on showed no indication of being anchored to the barn - rather the weight of the barn was holding it up.

A partial barn collapse. The walls of the barn did look to be anchored with a piece of rebarb sticking out of the concrete footers, and into a hole at the bottom of the 6x6 inch barn posts/vertical beams. No other anchoring clips were used, so wind was able to lift post off the anchor. The NWS Storm Survey Team also noted that most of the wood was dry rotted.
